alt: Rectangles with large coordinates become blocks of compressed cells. A grid of compressed cells shows, for each cell, how many rectangles cover it, and a table beside it gives the original width of each column and the original height of each row. Each step paints one rectangle onto the grid.

steps.caption: 3 rectangles have 6 distinct x values and 6 distinct y values, so the compressed grid has 5 columns and 5 rows. No cell is covered yet. Each column and row keeps the original distance between its two boundary coordinates.
Rectangle A has corner ranks columns 0 to 3 and rows 0 to 2. It covers the cells in columns 0 to 2 and rows 0 to 1: 6 cells.
Rectangle A is painted: every cell it covers went up by 1. Painting cell by cell costs one step for each cell of the rectangle.
Rectangle B has corner ranks columns 2 to 5 and rows 1 to 4. It covers the cells in columns 2 to 4 and rows 1 to 3: 9 cells.
Rectangle B is painted: every cell it covers went up by 1. Painting cell by cell costs one step for each cell of the rectangle.
Rectangle C has corner ranks columns 1 to 4 and rows 3 to 5. It covers the cells in columns 1 to 3 and rows 3 to 4: 6 cells.
Rectangle C is painted: every cell it covers went up by 1. Painting cell by cell costs one step for each cell of the rectangle.
All 3 rectangles are painted. The largest depth is 2; a cell with a 0 is not covered by any rectangle.
